assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies opened a new observational window, with a km3 detector built in Antarctic ice. It is original as an instrument and as a discovery, and the later associations with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane show lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: The supplied credit is a single name, Halzen, who conceived and led IceCube. A discovery of this scale rests on a large collaboration and on predecessors such as AMANDA, so a one-person prize would be a narrow reading of credit. I would want the committee to confirm whether other decisive figures are missing from the packet.
assessment.maturity: Strong. The diffuse flux has been confirmed across several event samples and by independent analyses, and the source associations add multimessenger corroboration. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Longlist credits only one person, and the collaboration and instrument-builder credit may be broader.
Individual source identification is still limited, so the astrophysical interpretation of the flux is incomplete.
I rely on memory of the IceCube results and have not verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fast X-ray localization of gamma-ray bursts with BeppoSAX, followed by optical and radio afterglows and redshifts, settled that bursts are cosmological, a decades-old puzzle. This is a clear instrument-enabled discovery with lasting impact on high-energy astrophysics and transient astronomy.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX instruments and the first afterglow detection. Kulkarni led the optical and radio follow-up and redshift work. The configuration is plausible, but Paczynski and van Paradijs (deceased) and the optical discovery teams complicate credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The result dates from 1997 and has been confirmed by Swift and many later missions. Recognition is arguably overdue, with the risk that time and mortality narrow the field.
uncertainties: Optical-detection credit is shared among several groups and the supplied names may not capture it.
Some key contributors are deceased and cannot be honoured.
I have not independently verified the discovery chronology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theoretical prediction and experimental realisation of topological insulators began a major field of condensed-matter physics with robust, widely confirmed consequences. It is original, clear and lasting. This is outside my own expertise, so I defer to colleagues on the finer points.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele predicted the quantum spin Hall effect, and Molenkamp's group observed it in HgTe quantum wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Hasan's work on three-dimensional topological insulators is an alternative fourth claim, and the omitted proposers (Bernevig, Zhang, Fu) may be disputed.
assessment.maturity: Mature. Many independent confirmations across materials, including ARPES and transport, have held up for fifteen years or more.
uncertainties: Credit is contested between the 2D and 3D discoveries and among several theorists, including some not on this entry.
Which of Mele, Molenkamp or Hasan is the most appropriate third laureate is an open question for the committee.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, reach fractional uncertainty near 1e-18. This is a precision-measurement advance with uses in geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and redefinition of the second. It is a clear instrument-led success.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the Sr clock. Ye's group pushed it to record stability and accuracy. Two names make a clean pair, but the 2005 prize to Hall and Hansch for frequency combs and the ion-clock work of Wineland already cover neighbouring ground.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature. Several independent labs reproduce the performance, but the redefinition of the second is still pending, so an application milestone is not yet reached.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes and with ion-clock and Ramsey-Borde-type work may weigh against it.
It is unclear whether the committee views the lattice clock as a distinct discovery or a refinement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of a non-zero theta13 was decisive for the three-flavour neutrino picture and opened the way to CP-violation searches. It is a clean, precise reactor and accelerator measurement.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang, Luk) and RENO reported the reactor result in 2012, and T2K (Nishikawa) gave the first accelerator appearance indication in 2011. Credit across Daya Bay, RENO and T2K is contested, and the longlist names omit RENO and Double Chooz leaders.
assessment.maturity: Mature and confirmed by several independent experiments, though the 2015 prize already honoured oscillations and the incremental weight of theta13 is smaller.
uncertainties: RENO and Double Chooz credit is not represented, and the three-name set may be unfair.
Whether a measurement of a mixing angle meets the discovery standard after the 2015 prize is arguable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background from pulsar timing is a new window on supermassive black-hole binaries. It rests on decades of precision timing, a technique I respect.
assessment.attribution: Pulsar timing array credit is spread across NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA and IPTA. The proposed three-name set is a thin subset of a large effort, and the origin of the signal is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Premature. The evidence is at about 3 to 4 sigma in several arrays, without a decisive Hellings-Downs detection at 5 sigma, and independent confirmation is still ongoing.
uncertainties: Significance and source interpretation (black-hole binaries or new physics) are unresolved.
Allocation of credit across the collaborations is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene produced flat bands, correlated insulators and unconventional superconductivity in a tunable platform and created a whole field of moire materials. It is original and highly consequential, though I would lean on condensed-matter colleagues.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle, and Jarillo-Herrero's group found the correlated states and superconductivity. Andrei's group made contributions that could also be considered, so a three-person limit leaves out a major claimant.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature. Many groups reproduce the phases, but the nature of the superconductivity is still debated, and the field may not be settled enough.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity is unresolved.
Credit for Andrei versus other experimental groups, and for earlier theory, is a possible dispute.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices allow quantum simulation of many-body models, such as the superfluid-Mott transition, with a precision and controllability not found elsewhere. It is a significant conceptual and experimental achievement, though it is outside my own field.
assessment.attribution: The theory credit (Zoller, Cirac, Jaksch) and experiment credit (Greiner, Bloch, Esslinger) can support several different three-person sets. Five names exceed the limit, so the committee must choose.
assessment.maturity: Mature in techniques, but quantum simulators are still reaching their scientific payoff, and the 2001 and 2012 prizes already cover neighbouring ground.
uncertainties: Allocation among five names is unresolved.
Overlap with earlier cold-atom prizes is a concern.
I rely on colleagues for judgement in this field.
